chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim said to him:
May my father and my mother be for you! Indeed, souls are approached in the morning and in the evening; so when that happens, then who will it be?
So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: When that happens, then he is your master.
And he struck with his hand upon the right shoulder of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, as far as I know; and he was, on that day, five years old, while Abdullah ibn Ja'far was sitting with us.

key_terms.الْأَنْفُسَ: the lives or souls of people, referring here to human mortality
key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: your master or leader, meaning the one who will hold authority over you
key_terms.مَنْكِبِ: shoulder, mentioned as the place upon which the Imam gestured
key_terms.يُرَاحُ: to be approached in the evening; paired with morning to convey constant vulnerability to death
key_terms.يُغْدَى: to be approached in the morning; here indicating the coming of death or changing conditions

ai.seo_question: How did Abu Abdullah عليه السلام indicate that Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام would be the next Imam?
ai.summary: This narration records a clear indication by Abu Abdullah عليه السلام toward the Imamate of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام after him. It highlights designation of religious authority within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and preserves a historical report about Imam Musa al-Kazim عليه السلام in his youth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Mansour Bin Hazim said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘

May by father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! The souls (people) wake up in the morning and they leave (die). So when it was that, so who (would be the next Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>)?’
So Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘When it would be like that, so it would be your master<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’,

and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> struck by his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> hand upon a shoulder of Abu Al-Hassan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> (7<sup style="font-weight: normal">th</sup> Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>), the right one as far as I know, and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, in those days, was five, and Abdullah, son of Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was seated along with us’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from Safwan al-Jammal from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.). Safwan has said the following. “Mansur ibn Hazim said to him, ‘
May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, the (human) souls pass through mornings and evenings if that (death for you) comes then who (will be the Imam)?”
Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) then said, “If that happens then he is your companion.”
He tapped the right shoulder of abu al-Hassan with his hand, as I know. He was five (feet tall or years old) at that time and ‘Abdallah ibn Ja‘far was also present with us.”
